title: When the Deadline Turns
premise: Lena Sterling, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Group—an embassy that exists on no map—has spent a decade erasing herself from every record. When a dead colleague's voiceprint unlocks a server in Tallinn, she learns the Group's founding director left her an inheritance: proof that her own agency is staging a catastrophic 'accident' at a Baltic summit to justify its continued existence. Hunted by the mentor who trained her and tethered by a ragtag crew of exiles she never meant to love, Lena must choose between the duty that made her and the family that found her. In the end she exposes the plot at the summit itself, burns the Meridian Group to the ground, and walks away invisible no longer—known, finally, by name.
about_author: Tamsin Halloran is a former diplomatic security consultant who spent eleven years in postings she still cannot name. She writes thrillers from a farmhouse in County Clare, where the go-bag is now full of dog treats.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A routine extraction in Vienna goes sideways when her handler orders her to abandon a source mid-operation. She complies—duty over conscience—but packs the man's daughter's drawing into her bag anyway. Emotional beat: the quiet cost of being someone who always follows orders.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. An anonymous file arrives containing a voiceprint of Marcus Vale, her mentor and the Group's legendary founder, presumed dead for six years. Speaking his own name into the mic unlocks a server in Tallinn. Emotional beat: grief re-opened like a wound.

chapters.title: What the Server Knew
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, intercut with encrypted logs. The inheritance: operational files proving the Group plans a staged attack—a gas leak 'accident' at the Riga Energy Summit—to secure a new mandate. Emotional beat: vertigo as her entire career reframes as complicity.

chapters.title: The Crew Nobody Assigned
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She reaches out to three people she's burned before: Sefa, a hacker living off-grid in Malta; Ilya, a disgraced summit security chief; and Noor, the abandoned source's daughter, now a journalist. Emotional beat: asking for help feels like weakness; it's actually the first brave thing.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The team meets in a shuttered fish cannery outside Valletta. Sefa decrypts the second layer of Vale's files while Lena realizes they're already being tracked. Emotional beat: wary strangers becoming, reluctantly, a unit.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Shadow
chapters.summary: Anton Reyes' POV—the current director and Lena's trainer. He reviews surveillance of the cannery and gives the kill order, then hesitates over Lena's file. Emotional beat: a man discovering that the instrument he built has developed a soul.

chapters.title: Twelve Days
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Countdown established: the summit opens in twelve days. Noor confirms a whistleblower inside the summit's host government is missing. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Malta Burns
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. The safehouse is hit. They escape through the cannery's flooded lower level, but Sefa's equipment—and half the evidence—is destroyed. Emotional beat: loss, and the discovery that losing things together binds people.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol, Personal
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Off the grid on a freighter to Athens, she trains the crew in tradecraft and admits, for the first time, what the Group took from her: a sister erased from every record for knowing too much. Emotional beat: vulnerability as strategy and as release.

chapters.title: The Missing Whistleblower
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In Athens, Noor traces the whistleblower to a private clinic—he's alive, sedated, and scheduled for 'transfer.' They extract him. Emotional beat: righteous fury tempered by care; Noor steps into her mother's unfinished fight.

chapters.title: Vale's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A hidden message from Marcus Vale reveals he faked his death to stop the plot from inside—and names the summit's trigger mechanism: a compromised ventilation control system. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed as responsibility, not treasure.

chapters.title: Riga, First Night
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. The crew infiltrates the summit venue using Ilya's old credentials. Lena comes face-to-face with Anton across a ballroom. Neither moves. Emotional beat: dread laced with something almost like mourning.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Anton's POV. Anton offers Lena everything: reinstatement, her sister's file, absolution—if she hands over Vale's server keys. She asks for twenty-four hours. Emotional beat: temptation rendered honestly; duty wearing the mask of mercy.

chapters.title: The Sister File
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Anton delivers on his word: her sister is alive, relocated, unremembering. Reading the file, Lena understands the offer's cruelty—it buys her silence with a life. Emotional beat: love against duty, weaponized.

chapters.title: Sefa's Gambit
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. With two days left, Sefa proposes broadcasting the evidence through the summit's own AV infrastructure—unblockable, undeniable. It requires physical access to the sealed control room. Emotional beat: the scared one volunteering for the scariest job.

chapters.title: Noor Goes Public
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor publishes the whistleblower's testimony early to force the Group's hand, blowing their timeline but flushing out the operation's field team. Emotional beat: courage that looks like recklessness until it works.

chapters.title: Vent Nine
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Summit eve. Lena crawls the maintenance spine to reach the ventilation controls and finds them already armed—someone moved the schedule up. Emotional beat: cold clarity under maximum pressure.

chapters.title: The Man Who Made Her
chapters.summary: Lena and Anton POV, alternating. Confrontation in the control room: guns, history, and Anton's confession that Vale's death order was his first act as director. Lena disarms him without killing him. Emotional beat: breaking from the maker without becoming a destroyer.

chapters.title: Accident, Cancelled
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. As delegates fill the plenary hall, Sefa hijacks the screens, Ilya locks down the vents, and Noor's story breaks worldwide. The 'accident' dies unborn in front of its intended audience. Emotional beat: triumph that tastes like exhaustion.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Meridian
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Governments descend; the Group is dismantled in real time. Anton, arrested, tells her Vale would be proud. Lena watches the machine that made her get fed into the shredder. Emotional beat: liberation and bereavement in the same breath.

chapters.title: Known by Name
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In a Dublin café, Lena meets her sister—no cover story, no alias, just her name spoken aloud by family. The go-bag stays unpacked by the door. Emotional beat: the found family and the lost one merging into one table.

chapters.title: The Next Signal
chapters.summary: Epilogue, rotating POVs. Months later, an encrypted ping arrives from an unknown server—Vale's voiceprint again, or someone imitating it. The crew, scattered across three countries, all open the file at once. Emotional beat: the door left open; family answers together or not at all.
